headline_en: Secondary Bond market yields see-saw; recover to close steady to higher | Daily FT
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Secondary Bond market yields see-saw; recover to close steady to higher | Daily FT
summary_en: The secondary Bond market initially commenced the trading week ending 23 October on a distinctly bearish footing, with aggressive selling interest driving yields sharply higher and extending the upward momentum from the previous week.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. The secondary Bond market initially commenced the trading week ending 23 October on a distinctly bearish footing, with aggressive selling interest driving yields sharply higher and extending the upward momentum from the previous week.
content: The secondary Bond market initially commenced the trading week ending 23 October on a distinctly bearish footing, with aggressive selling interest driving yields sharply higher and extending the upward momentum from the previous week. However, the elevated yield levels attracted strong buying interest, which absorbed the selling pressure and provided firm support to the market. Traded volumes increased significantly as demand emerged at the higher levels. This paved the way for a recovery through the middle of the week, with yields reversing their initial increases and declining across medium to longer tenors amid sustained buying interest. Activity and traded volumes remained healthy, reflecting improved demand at the recently elevated levels. Buying interest subsequently centred on the shorter 2028–2031 maturities, driving yields lower at the short end, while the remainder of the curve held broadly steady. Activity moderated towards the close of the week. Despite this recovery, two-way quotes closed slightly higher on the belly end of the curve after recovering from their intraweek highs while the short end remained steady, week on week. At the very short end of the curve, the 15.12.26 touched an intraweek high of 9.50% before trading down to a low of 9.42%, while the 15.01.27 traded at 9.50%. The 15.09.29 and 15.12.29 traded at 11.10% and 11.15% respectively. The 15.05.30 traded at 11.40%, while the 01.07.30 traded down from an intraweek high of 11.65% to a low of 11.50%. The 01.08.30 saw its yield ease off from 11.60%-11.50% while the 15.10.30 traded down the range of 11.65% to 11.55%. The 15.01.33 traded up to a high of 12.30% before easing to 12.17%, subsequent to hitting a weekly low of 12.10%. The 2031 and 2034 tenors exhibited the see-saw movement more profoundly, with the 01.02.31 and 01.12.31 increasing to weekly highs of 11.80% and 11.95% respectively from 11.65% and 11.80% opening lows before easing to 11.75% and 11.85% at the end of the week. All three 2034 tenors (15.06.34, 15.09.34 & 15.10.34) followed suit, increasing from an opening average low of 12.33% to highs of 12.55% and easing to close the week on 2-way quotes of 12.35%/12.45% across all the maturities. The 15.03.35 traded at 12.55%. At the weekly Treasury Bill auction conducted last Wednesday (21), weighted average yields were seen holding broadly steady for a second consecutive week with the rate on the 182-day and 364-day tenors remaining unchanged at 9.44% and 9.95% respectively for the second straight week. However, the 91-day tenor maturity saw its yield edge up marginally by 02 basis points to 9.32%. The Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) raised only Rs. 80.611 billion or 80.61% in total out of the Rs. 100 billion offered in total. The 91-day tenor recorded acceptance above its respective target allocation, while the 182-day and 364-day recorded acceptances below their respective offered amounts. Total bids received amounted to 1.86 times the overall offer. Meanwhile, the foreign holdings of rupee-denominated Government securities recorded a net outflow for the first time in four weeks, registering a decrease amounting 1.40% or Rs. 2.82 billion for the week ended 22 October. Accordingly, the total foreign holdings of rupee treasuries decreased to Rs. 199.54 billion. The Surplus liquidity in money markets was seen remaining elevated for the week ending 23 October 2026, at Rs. 384.90 billion albeit declining slightly as compared to its previous week’s closing level of Rs. 399.88 billion. The weighted average rates on Call Money and Repo closed last week at 9.00% and 9.06% as against 8.99% and 9.04% respectively the previous week. Furthermore, the rupee or the USD/LKR rate was seen depreciating, to close the week ending 23 October at Rs. 332.10/332.20 as against its previous week’s closing of Rs. 331.25/331.35. This was subsequent to trading within an intraweek high of Rs. 331.35 and a low of Rs. 332.26 intraweek. The average daily USD/LKR traded volume over the first four trading days of the week stood at $ 51.67 million. (References: Public Debt Management Office - Ministry of Finance, Central Bank of Sri Lanka, Bloomberg E-Bond Trading Platform, Money Broking Companies)

headline_en: LankaQR Rs. 51 Million Lucky Draw to Debut on 27 October
headline_si: රුපියල් මිලියන 51ක LankaQR වාසනා දිනුම් ඇදීම ඔක්තෝබර් 27 දා ඇරඹේ
summary_en: The registration-free national LankaQR Lucky Draw is scheduled to be launched on 27 October 2026 to reward customers and merchants using QR payments. Transactions completed from 1 September 2026 to 28 February 2027 will be entered automatically into weekly and monthly draws offering a total prize pool estimated at Rs. 51 million. The draws will be administered by LankaPay with GovTech support and overseen by a multi-agency Draw Committee.
summary_si: LankaQR ගෙවීම් භාවිත කරන ගනුදෙනුකරුවන් සහ වෙළෙඳුන්ට ත්‍යාග පිරිනැමීම සඳහා ලියාපදිංචියකින් තොර ජාතික වාසනා දිනුම් ඇදීම 2026 ඔක්තෝබර් 27 දා ආරම්භ කිරීමට නියමිතය. 2026 සැප්තැම්බර් 1 සිට 2027 පෙබරවාරි 28 දක්වා සිදු කෙරෙන ගනුදෙනු, රුපියල් මිලියන 51ක් ලෙස ඇස්තමේන්තු කර ඇති සමස්ත ත්‍යාග අරමුදලක් සහිත සතිපතා සහ මාසික දිනුම් ඇදීම් සඳහා ස්වයංක්‍රීයව ඇතුළත් කෙරේ. GovTech සහාය ඇතිව LankaPay විසින් දිනුම් ඇදීම් ක්‍රියාත්මක කෙරෙන අතර, බහු ආයතනික දිනුම් ඇදීම් කමිටුවක් විසින් ඒවා අධීක්ෂණය කෙරේ.
content:
The national QR payment adoption program’s Lucky Draw is set to be launched, with the first draws scheduled for 27 October 2026. The registration-free nationwide draw has been designed to encourage and reward the everyday use of LankaQR payments by customers and merchants.

All transactions completed between 1 September 2026 and 28 February 2027 will be treated as eligible. Every customer or merchant who has used LankaQR since 1 September 2026 will be considered automatically, allowing participation without a separate registration process.

Two types of cash prizes will be offered. Under the weekly draw, Rs. 5,000 will be awarded to each of 250 weekly winners. Under the monthly grand draw, Rs. 1,000,000 will be awarded to two winners, Rs. 500,000 to two winners and Rs. 250,000 to two winners.

For each weekly draw, 250 winners will be selected, comprising 125 merchants and 125 customers. For each monthly grand draw, six winners will be selected, comprising three customers and three merchants. Across the six-month period, the total prize pool has been estimated at Rs. 51,000,000.

Each eligible LankaQR transaction will qualify both parties for entry into both draws. Person-to-merchant transactions and person-to-person transactions will both be treated as eligible. All prizes will be credited directly to the winners’ bank accounts.

For a given month, all four weekly draws and the monthly draw will be held during the following month. On 27 October 2026, four weekly draws and one monthly grand draw covering September will be conducted.

The draws will be based on transaction data received from participating banks. They will be run by LankaPay and supported by GovTech.

For transparency, every draw will be overseen by a designated Draw Committee. The committee will comprise at least one representative each from the Ministry of Digital Economy; the Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development; the Central Bank of Sri Lanka; and the Auditor General’s Department.

Winners will be announced within two weeks through their respective banks, while information on prize-pool distribution will be provided via the Ministry of Digital Economy and GovTech.

headline_en: Amana Bank Opens 50th Self-Banking Centre in Grandpass
headline_si: අමානා බැංකුව ග්‍රෑන්ඩ්පාස්හි 50 වැනි ස්වයං බැංකුකරණ මධ්‍යස්ථානය විවෘත කරයි
summary_en: Amana Bank’s 50th Self Banking Centre has been opened in Grandpass, Colombo, as the Bank celebrates its 15th Anniversary. Its customer footprint has thereby been expanded to 83 locations, including 33 fully fledged branches. Around-the-clock access to cash withdrawals, cash and cheque deposits, and bill payments will be provided to businesses and residents in the area.
summary_si: අමානා බැංකුව සිය 15 වැනි සංවත්සරය සමරන අතරතුර එහි 50 වැනි ස්වයං බැංකුකරණ මධ්‍යස්ථානය කොළඹ ග්‍රෑන්ඩ්පාස්හි විවෘත කර ඇත. ඒ අනුව, පූර්ණ පහසුකම් සහිත ශාඛා 33ක් ඇතුළුව බැංකුවේ පාරිභෝගික සේවා ස්ථාන සංඛ්‍යාව 83 දක්වා පුළුල් කර තිබේ. මුදල් ආපසු ගැනීම්, මුදල් හා චෙක්පත් තැන්පතු සහ බිල්පත් ගෙවීම් ඇතුළු අත්‍යවශ්‍ය බැංකු සේවා සඳහා පැය 24 පුරා ප්‍රවේශය ප්‍රදේශයේ ව්‍යාපාරිකයන්ට සහ පදිංචිකරුවන්ට සලසා දෙනු ඇත.
content:
Amana Bank’s customer location network has been further expanded through the opening of its 50th Self Banking Centre in Grandpass, Colombo, with another significant milestone being marked as the Bank celebrates its 15th Anniversary. The new Self Banking Centre was officially unveiled by Amana Bank Managing Director/CEO Mohamed Azmeer together with Senior Vice President - Chief Compliance Officer Ajmal Naleer, Senior Vice President - Business Banking Irshad Iqbal, Vice President – Retail Banking and Marketing Siddeeque Akbar and other senior officials of the Bank.

With this opening, Amana Bank’s footprint has been increased to 83 customer locations, including 33 fully fledged branches. The new Self Banking Centre has been located within the vibrant and commercially active Grandpass area and has been positioned to serve the diverse banking needs of the locality’s growing business and residential communities.

As Grandpass is home to a wide range of commercial establishments, entrepreneurs, traders and residents, greater convenience and 24x7 accessibility to essential banking services will be provided to customers in the area through Amana Bank’s presence. These services include cash withdrawals, cash deposits, cheque deposits and bill payments.

The significance of the milestone was highlighted by Amana Bank Managing Director/CEO Mohamed Azmeer, who said: “The Opening of our 50th Self Banking Centre during our 15th Anniversary year is a significant milestone for the Bank. Over the last five years, we have increasingly invested in our Self Banking Centre model as an effective way of extending our reach which has enabled us to bring essential banking services closer to more communities, while responding to the growing preference for convenient, self-service banking. The success of our Self Banking Centre initiative has become an important part of our commitment to making our Development Focused, People Friendly Banking model more accessible to customers and communities across the country. Grandpass is a vibrant commercial and residential hub with a strong community of businesses, entrepreneurs and residences. We are honoured to establish our 50th Self Banking Centre in Grandpass.”

headline_en: Assetline Finance Expands Network with 64th Branch in Wattala
headline_si: ඇසට්ලයින් ෆිනෑන්ස් සිය 64 වැනි ශාඛාව වත්තලදී විවෘත කරයි
summary_en: Assetline Finance PLC’s 64th branch has been opened at No. 58/1/1, Old Negombo Road, Wattala, to provide local communities and businesses with convenient access to financial services. Vehicle financing, auto loans, asset drafts, solar financing and personalised financial advice will be offered through the new facility. A nationwide network of 64 dedicated branches is now operated by AFIN, supported by more than 2,500 touchpoints maintained through the David Pieris Group.

headline_en: AIA Sri Lanka Advances Project NOVA with iAcademy Launch
headline_si: iAcademy දියත් කරමින් AIA ශ්‍රී ලංකා Project NOVA පරිවර්තන ගමන ඉදිරියට ගෙන යයි
summary_en: iAcademy, a next-generation digital learning platform, has been launched by AIA Sri Lanka to modernise the onboarding and training of new Wealth Planners under Project NOVA. Location-based training has been transformed into a structured, self-paced online experience featuring trilingual support, licensing guidance and real-time progress monitoring. The wider onboarding process is automatically advanced once all required modules have been successfully completed.
summary_si: Project NOVA යටතේ නව Wealth Planners සඳහා වන බඳවාගැනීමේ හා පුහුණු ක්‍රියාවලිය නවීකරණය කිරීම සඳහා AIA ශ්‍රී ලංකා විසින් ඊළඟ පරම්පරාවේ ඩිජිටල් ඉගෙනුම් වේදිකාවක් වන iAcademy දියත් කර ඇත. ස්ථානගත පුහුණුව, ත්‍රෛභාෂා සහාය, බලපත්‍ර විභාග මාර්ගෝපදේශනය සහ තත්‍ය කාලීන ප්‍රගති අධීක්ෂණය සහිත ව්‍යුහගත, ස්වයං වේගී මාර්ගගත අත්දැකීමක් බවට පරිවර්තනය කර ඇත. අවශ්‍ය සියලුම මොඩියුල සාර්ථකව සම්පූර්ණ කළ පසු බඳවාගැනීමේ ක්‍රියාවලිය ස්වයංක්‍රීයව ඉදිරියට ගෙන යනු ලැබේ.
content:
iAcademy, a next-generation digital learning platform designed to simplify and modernise the onboarding and training experience for new Wealth Planners, has been launched by AIA Sri Lanka. Another significant milestone in the company’s transformation journey through Project NOVA has thereby been marked.

Through iAcademy, traditionally location-based training programs have been transformed into a digital experience that can be accessed online, anytime and anywhere. Training can now be completed by AIA Wealth Planners at their own pace, while a consistent and structured onboarding experience is provided.

The essential knowledge and capabilities required by new Wealth Planners to begin their careers with AIA are provided through the platform. An introduction to values and culture is included in the learning journey, together with comprehensive product knowledge, insurance fundamentals, an understanding of the Wealth Planner profession and its benefits, sales processes and best practices, and compliance and regulatory requirements.

An interactive orientation learning experience and licensing examination guidance are also included in iAcademy, with trilingual language support being provided. The platform has also been designed to extend beyond digital learning by helping to streamline the wider onboarding journey.

Real-time visibility of training progress and completion status is provided through iAcademy. Upon the successful completion of all required modules, the onboarding process is automatically advanced.

The following statement was made by AIA Sri Lanka Deputy CEO /Chief Distribution Officer Upul Wijesinghe: “By harnessing technology, we are creating a faster, simpler and more accessible onboarding experience that gives our Wealth Planners greater flexibility in how they learn, while equipping them with the knowledge and confidence they need to succeed from day one.”

The following statement was made by Chief Agency Officer Dimuthu Piyasena: “Our Wealth Planners are central to the way we connect with and serve our customers. iAcademy allows us to deliver a structured and engaging learning experience while giving new Wealth Planners the flexibility to learn at their own pace.”

As AIA Sri Lanka’s transformation through Project NOVA is continued, another step towards the creation of a more digitally enabled agency force is represented by iAcademy. At the same time, new Wealth Planners are being provided with the knowledge, tools and confidence required to succeed from the outset.

summary_en: The National Public Service Dialogue Forum was launched last week by the Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Ministry in partnership with the International Labour Organisation. A three-tier framework was established for workplace concerns and grievances to be addressed at workplace, sectoral and national levels. Improved accountability, institutional resilience, social cohesion and uninterrupted public service delivery are expected to be supported through the initiative.
summary_si: රාජ්‍ය පරිපාලන, පළාත් සභා සහ පළාත් පාලන අමාත්‍යාංශය හා ජාත්‍යන්තර කම්කරු සංවිධානය එක්ව ජාතික රාජ්‍ය සේවා සංවාද සංසදය පසුගිය සතියේ දියත් කරන ලදී. සේවා ස්ථාන ගැටලු සහ දුක්ගැනවිලි සේවා ස්ථාන, ආංශික සහ ජාතික මට්ටම්වලදී විසඳීම සඳහා ත්‍රි-මට්ටම් රාමුවක් ස්ථාපිත කර ඇත. මෙම වැඩපිළිවෙළ මඟින් වගවීම, ආයතනික ප්‍රත්‍යස්ථතාව, සමාජ ඒකාබද්ධතාව සහ බාධාවකින් තොර රාජ්‍ය සේවා සැපයීම ශක්තිමත් කිරීමට අපේක්ෂා කෙරේ.
content:
The Declaration on Social Dialogue in the Public Service was handed over to Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake by Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Ministry Secretary S. Alokabandara, pictured on the left, at the launch of the National Public Service Forum.

The National Public Service Dialogue Forum was launched last week by the Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Ministry in partnership with the International Labour Organisation (ILO). Through the Forum, a formal and structured space is provided for government administrators and public service employees across the country to discuss workplace issues and concerns.

Workplace challenges and grievances are intended to be addressed through dialogue and joint problem-solving. Through improved workplace relations and strengthened accountability, a contribution is expected to be made towards a more responsive and resilient public service.

The framework is structured across three levels—workplace, sectoral and national—so that issues can be addressed at the appropriate level. Issues within individual institutions are dealt with by workplace forums, while matters that cannot be resolved at that level can be referred to sectoral forums. Issues affecting more than one sector or requiring action by central government authorities are addressed by the National forum.

The following statement was made by Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government Ministry Secretary S. Alokabandara: “The National Public Service Dialogue Forum gives administrators and employees a permanent space to raise concerns early and resolve them together, so that services to citizens continue without interruption. It can also help ensure that reforms, including digitalization and training, take account of the experience of the people responsible for delivering public services.”

It has already been demonstrated through established workplace forums how dialogue was used to address challenges ranging from promotion processes to workplace safety, while ways to strengthen organizational performance and improve service delivery were identified. content:
Prices of several upcountry and low-country vegetables have increased amid prevailing rainy weather, with traders warning that prices could rise further as the festive season approaches.

The wholesale price of tomatoes, which ranged between Rs. 350 and Rs. 400 per kilogram last week, has climbed to between Rs. 600 and Rs. 650.

The price of capsicum has also increased from Rs. 250 to between Rs. 400 and Rs. 450 per kilogram, while the wholesale price of cabbage has risen from Rs. 150 to Rs. 350.

Former Chief Organiser of the Manning Market Traders Union Anil Indrajith said adverse weather conditions were the main reason for the recent price increases and warned that prices could continue to rise in the coming weeks.

“Vegetable prices have increased these days. The main reason for this is the prevailing weather conditions in the country. Tomatoes are currently the most expensive, with wholesale prices reaching around Rs. 600 per kilogram,” he said.

Indrajith said beans were selling at between Rs. 400 and Rs. 500 per kilogram, while carrots were priced between Rs. 200 and Rs. 250. Leeks were selling at Rs. 200 per kilogram, and green chillies ranged between Rs. 350 and Rs. 400.

Prices of low-country vegetables have also increased, with snake gourd selling at around Rs. 400 per kilogram and ridge gourd priced between Rs. 200 and Rs. 250. A kilogram of pumpkin was selling for more than Rs. 200.

Only vegetables such as ash gourd and cucumber remained available at prices below Rs. 100 per kilogram, he said.

“Overall, vegetable prices have increased compared to last month. Generally, vegetable prices tend to rise every year as December approaches. Therefore, a price reduction cannot be expected in the coming period, and prices could increase further,” Indrajith added.

Meanwhile, All-Island Poultry Association Chairman Ajith Gunasekara said market purchases of eggs and chicken had declined by around 20%, reflecting reduced consumer purchasing power amid prevailing economic conditions.

He noted that the production cost of an egg ranged between Rs. 30 and Rs. 32, while farms were currently selling eggs at similar prices, leaving producers with little opportunity to make a profit.

Gunasekara also said chicken consumption had declined, with prices falling amid weaker demand.

“Consumers’ purchasing power has declined at present. When we conduct market surveys, we can see that purchases of eggs and chicken have decreased. We observe that consumption in the market has declined by around 20%,” he said.

“The production cost of an egg is generally between Rs. 30 and Rs. 32. However, farms are currently releasing eggs at prices ranging between Rs. 30 and Rs. 32 as well. Therefore, producers are not in a profitable position,” he added.

Despite the decline in demand, Gunasekara said poultry production was continuing without interruption and that steps were being taken to maintain adequate supplies of eggs and chicken throughout the festive season without shortages.

The association expressed hope that market conditions would return to normal with the start of the festive season after November 15.

On 15 October, the Presidential Secretariat was surrounded by protesting monks, after which the protest was moved to Viharamahadevi Park, where it was temporarily paused yesterday.

The satyagraha at Viharamahadevi Park in Colombo, through which the release of Bodu Bala Sena General Secretary Ven. Galagodaatte Gnanasara Thero was demanded, was temporarily suspended yesterday, according to Ven. Ulapane Sumangala Thero.

The media was addressed yesterday afternoon by Ven. Sumangala Thero alongside the Buddhist monks participating in the satyagraha. It was stated that the decision had been taken following information that intervention was being made by the Mahanayake Theros of the Three Nikayas to secure the release of Ven. Gnanasara Thero.

A call was issued yesterday by the Mahanayake Theros of the Three Nikayas for Buddhist monks to uphold monastic discipline and harmony. A warning was also issued that ongoing protests demanding a presidential pardon for Ven. Galagodaatte Gnanasara Thero were being exploited by certain groups to damage the reputation of the Buddhist clergy locally and internationally.

In a special statement, it was said by the senior prelates that intervention had already been made and discussions had been initiated with the Government for the matter to be resolved through legal means and dialogue.

It was further stated that the respect accorded to Buddhist monks within Sri Lanka’s religious and social context was dependent on the preservation of monastic discipline, or Vinaya, and spiritual restraint.

Members of the Maha Sangha, the order of Buddhist monks, across all Nikayas were called upon by the prelates to maintain unity and harmony within the clergy. They were also urged to ensure that disputes were resolved in accordance with the Dhamma and Vinaya and that conduct strengthening public confidence and faith was maintained.

The statement was issued by Siam Nikaya Malwathu Chapter Mahanayake Most Ven. Tibbatuwawe Sri Siddhartha Sumangala Thero, Siam Nikaya Asgiri Chapter Mahanayake Most Ven. Warakagoda Sri Pannananda Dhammasiddhi Thero, Sri Lanka Amarapura Nikaya Supreme Mahanayake Most Ven. Karagoda Uyangoda Maithree Moorthi Thero and Sri Lanka Ramanna Nikaya Mahanayake Most Ven. Makulawewa Sri Wimala Thero.

headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: British Airways celebrates return to Sri Lanka with special fares | Daily FT
summary_en: British Airways on Saturday marked a significant milestone with the arrival of its first flight into Colombo, reconnecting Sri Lanka with the UK for the first time in over 11 years.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. British Airways on Saturday marked a significant milestone with the arrival of its first flight into Colombo, reconnecting Sri Lanka with the UK for the first time in over 11 years.
content:
British Airways Captain Terry Smith and Hayleys Chairman and Chief Executive Mohan Pandithage cut a cake to celebrate the resumption of direct services on Saturday. British High Commissioner Andrew Patrick, British Airways General Manager – South Asia David Wright, Civil Aviation Authority Director General and CEO Capt. Daminda Rambukwella, British Airways Senior First Officer Pradeeb Vimalraj, IAG Cargo Regional Commercial Manager – Asia Pacific, India and Middle East Ankush Chawla and Hayleys Advantis Managing Director Ruwan Waidyaratne are among those who look on

British Airways General Manager – South Asia David Wright

British Airways Captain Terry Smith (third from left), Senior First Officer Preveen Moorthy (left), and IAG Cargo Regional Commercial Manager – Asia Pacific, India and Middle East Ankush Chawla (right)

The crew of the first British Airways flight

British Airways on Saturday marked a significant milestone with the arrival of its first flight into Colombo, reconnecting Sri Lanka with the UK for the first time in over 11 years. The inaugural flight, operated by Sri Lankan crew, was welcomed by traditional dancers and drummers on arrival to commemorate the occasion. The new route strengthens links between the two countries, supporting tourism, trade, and business travel. The thrice-weekly service will be operated by British Airways’ Boeing 777 fleet, featuring Club World (business class), World Traveller Plus (premium economy), and World Traveller (economy) cabins. To celebrate the launch, British Airways is offering special return fares with savings of up to 10% in World Traveller, starting from Rs. 255,000 for travel from Colombo to London Gatwick. British Airways Chief Planning and Strategy Officer Neil Chernoff in a statement said the resumption marks a special moment for British Airways, as it meant bringing Sri Lanka back to its global network and giving customers greater choice when planning their next getaway. “Sri Lanka is renowned for its warmth, rich culture, and hospitality, and we’re delighted to be flying there once again. To celebrate, we’re offering special fares and look forward to welcoming customers on board,” he added. Noting that Sri Lanka is one of the first re-entries in recent months, British Airways General Manager – South Asia David Wright during a media interaction post-first flight on Saturday stressed that Sri Lanka has always been a really important market for British Airways. “Between the UK and Sri Lanka, we have deep cultural and historic links, and so it is a market that we continue to keep an eye on. And obviously, over the last few years, we have seen that economic growth and tourism rebound post-COVID, and we continue to review our network, and we felt that the time was right to reintroduce our services from this winter,” he told journalists in Colombo. Wright said that a heart of a business case like this is very much tourism from the UK coming into the incredible island of Sri Lanka and everything it has to offer. “But we have also seen really positive demand across sectors: tourism going into the UK, but also across business sectors and also people visiting communities and friends and family as well.” He described the all-inclusive offers starting from Rs. 255,000 as “compelling.” The Boeing 777 has a capacity of over 300 seats and Wright noted that British Airways has been really pleased with the response. The special fares in World Traveller (economy) on return flights from Colombo to Gatwick, available for booking until 15 November 2026, for outbound travel between 20 October and 30 November 2026 and inbound travel between 26 October and 10 December 2026. British Airways General Sales Agents (GSA) Hayleys Advantis Ltd., Managing Director Ruwan Waidyaratne said: “The commencement of British Airways’ flight operations to Colombo marks a significant milestone in enhancing air connectivity between Sri Lanka and the UK. The service will offer customers greater travel options while supporting tourism and business travel between the two markets, and we look forward to continuing our partnership with British Airways.” He said Hayleys’ relationship with British Airways dates back to 1995, and it is delighted to welcome the airline back to Sri Lanka as this longstanding partnership enters a new chapter. Waidyaratne stressed that improved connectivity between Sri Lanka and the UK creates opportunities that extends beyond travel, supporting tourism, stimulating economic activities, and strengthening ties between the two countries. “We look forward to seeing this connection grow and deliver lasting value for travellers, the tourism industry, and Sri Lanka as a whole,” he added. Senior First Officer Pradeeb Vimalraj, who operated the airline’s inaugural flight in a statement said: “As a Sri Lankan, born and raised in Jaffna in my early years, bringing our first flight back home after more than a decade was particularly special. The warm welcome we received made it even more memorable, and I am so proud to be part of this new chapter connecting Sri Lanka and the UK.” British Airways also revealed that searches on ba.com for flights from London to Colombo have increased by more than 10% in the past week, reflecting continued interest in the destination. British Airways operates one of the largest and the most modern fleets of any airline in the world and is transforming the operations with a £ 7 billion investment plan. Departure from Gatwick is at 1640 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays and arrival in Colombo at 0935 hours the next day. Departure from Colombo is 1035 hours Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays with arrival at Gatwick at 1700 hours. British Airways said the new service gives customers travelling from the UK direct access to one of South Asia’s most captivating destinations. From golden beaches and ancient cultural sites to wildlife reserves, tea country and a thriving food scene, Sri Lanka offers a diverse range of experiences for travellers to discover.

summary_en: Sri Lanka can revive stalled negotiations on the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India by first concluding a standalone Digital Economy Agreement that builds on the momentum of recent bilateral digital cooperation, Centre for a Smart Future (CSF) Co-Founder and Economist Anushka Wijesinha said.

Sri Lanka can revive stalled negotiations on the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India by first concluding a standalone Digital Economy Agreement that builds on the momentum of recent bilateral digital cooperation, Centre for a Smart Future (CSF) Co-Founder and Economist Anushka Wijesinha said.
content:
CSF Co-Founder and Economist Anushka Wijesinha

Sri Lanka can revive stalled negotiations on the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India by first concluding a standalone Digital Economy Agreement that builds on the momentum of recent bilateral digital cooperation, Centre for a Smart Future (CSF) Co-Founder and Economist Anushka Wijesinha said. Wijesinha noted that the ETCA negotiations had dragged through 14 rounds over many years and multiple governments, with momentum slowing significantly on the Sri Lankan side. The present Government is awaiting the completion of a unilateral review of existing free trade agreements (FTAs) before deciding how to proceed with any new ones, while the ETCA and its predecessor, Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), carry political baggage as initiatives inherited from previous administrations. Against this backdrop, he said digital connectivity had been driving a new phase in bilateral relations. Initiatives around digital payments integration led by India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), collaboration on digital public infrastructure, especially the digital ID project, and the emergence of trade settlement in Indian and Sri Lankan rupees have characterised this phase, building on India’s 2022 crisis-era assistance and relief following Cyclone Ditwah. “Carving some of these initiatives out into an immediate, standalone Digital Economy Agreement can capture this momentum,” Wijesinha said. He argued that converting ad hoc, episodic initiatives into mutually negotiated commitments, with defined obligations and review mechanisms, would place digital cooperation within a firm institutional framework. “An achievable ‘early harvest’ win here would inject fresh enthusiasm into Indo-Lanka economic integration, while demonstrating tangible benefits to domestic stakeholders,” he said. Wijesinha pointed out that such a modular approach would not be unprecedented. India has already decided to unbundle investment chapters from comprehensive FTAs, expecting partners instead to sign Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) based on its Model BIT. This has been conveyed to Sri Lanka, and a new standalone BIT is expected to be signed rather than an investment chapter being included in the ETCA, as the Sri Lankan side had previously assumed. Applying the same precedent to the digital sphere, he said, would allow both nations to advance high-value integration without getting bogged down by traditional trade bottlenecks. For design, he suggested the two countries look to ASEAN’s Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), recently concluded and now awaiting ratification by Member States. The DEFA grew out of each member economy’s post-COVID push towards digitalisation, expanding into a pan-regional ambition from 2023. While acknowledging that sceptics might dismiss a 10-nation regional treaty as irrelevant to a bilateral relationship, Wijesinha said DEFA’s core value lay in how it navigated differences in scale and readiness among its members. Instead of demanding full regulatory harmonisation, which often triggers concerns over sovereignty and dominance, the framework relied on interoperability, tiering, sequencing, and flexible commitments. “Rather than requiring Sri Lanka to harmonise its laws and systems to Indian standards, a DEFA-inspired interoperability approach would allow divergent national systems to recognise and transact with each other without enforcing identical rules,” he said, adding that this could be backed by tiered and possibly sequenced commitments, with periodic reviews allowing ambition to grow over time. DEFA covers nine areas, ranging from payments and digital ID to cybersecurity, data flows, competition policy and talent mobility. However, Wijesinha said an India-Sri Lanka agreement need not cover all of these at once, and should focus on practical, non-controversial areas where collaboration is already underway or imminent. These include payment system interoperability, digital trade and paperless customs, treatment of cross-border e-commerce and digital goods, mutual legal recognition of e-signatures, cybersecurity cooperation, and cooperation on emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI). Sensitive areas that risk stalling negotiations could be excluded, he said. Talent mobility is politically sensitive in Sri Lanka, and DEFA’s provisions on the preferential movement of digital talent and entrepreneurs are possible in ASEAN partly because labour mobility is less politically charged among its members. In Sri Lanka, liberalising Mode 4 services, which covers professionals temporarily crossing borders to deliver services, attracts considerable domestic sensitivity, as earlier CEPA and ETCA rounds showed. Cross-border data flows are similarly difficult to model directly on DEFA’s default of free flow, he noted. India’s data protection regime leans towards retaining the ability to impose sector-specific data localisation requirements, while Sri Lanka is only just advancing its own data protection regime. Wijesinha stressed that negotiating a digital agreement first did not mean abandoning the broader ambition for a comprehensive deal such as the ETCA, but could instead serve as a stimulant to the stalled process. He recalled that when the CEPA was envisioned, the Joint Study Group showed bold ambition by mapping extensive cooperation areas beyond goods trade, just three years after the first bilateral agreement came into force. While such ambition and foresight appear to have dipped since, he said decoupling the digital agenda and forging a dedicated agreement could rekindle that forward-looking spirit, bring in new stakeholders and reflect contemporary aspirations on both sides. “India and Sri Lanka must not let legacy trade hurdles hurt optimism for new areas of economic integration,” Wijesinha said. He made these observations in an article for the Observer Research Foundation (https://www.orfonline.org/expert-speak/can-a-digital-economy-agreement-refresh-india-sri-lanka-economic-integration).

headline_en: Finalise ETCA with India before other trade deals: Ranil | Daily FT
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Finalise ETCA with India before other trade deals: Ranil | Daily FT
summary_en: EX- President Ranil Wickremesinghe has called for Sri Lanka to finalise the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India as its first trade priority, ahead of free trade agreements (FTAs) with other Asian economies.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. EX- President Ranil Wickremesinghe has called for Sri Lanka to finalise the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India as its first trade priority, ahead of free trade agreements (FTAs) with other Asian economies.
content:
EX- President Ranil Wickremesinghe has called for Sri Lanka to finalise the Economic and Technology Cooperation Agreement (ETCA) with India as its first trade priority, ahead of free trade agreements (FTAs) with other Asian economies.

“Our first one is that we have to do the agreement with India,” Wickremesinghe said, noting that the agreement was currently suspended. He was speaking at the 50th webinar organised by the Daily FT, Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), and the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka, together with Women in Management (WIM), the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors, the MBA Alumni Association of the University of Colombo, and Pioneer Institute of Business and Technology, on Saturday.

Asked whether India would change the global order, Wickremesinghe said that while the order currently appeared to rest on the US, China, and Russia, India could not be ignored. “It’s going to be the third-largest GDP in the world. It’s a military power and it is the dominant power in the Indian Ocean. So at some stage, India has to come in,” he said. The US, he noted, had also improved relations with Pakistan, and how it balanced these relationships would matter. On managing relations with India and China, he said Sri Lanka and India were close and should be closer, keeping the spirit of the exchange of letters between Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene that neither country would do anything to harm the security of the other. Relations had evolved since the time of Emperor Ashoka according to developments in the world, he said. “Now, it’s not a question of India or China, it’s how India and China manage their relationships,” he said. With China set to enter the Bay of Bengal, Myanmar and Bangladesh would become places of competing influence, he added, noting that India was strengthening its friendship with Myanmar and that both India and China, as BRICS members, would have to reach an understanding on how the region developed.

headline_en: Experts outline Sri Lanka’s priorities in new world order | Daily FT
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Experts outline Sri Lanka’s priorities in new world order | Daily FT
summary_en: Sri Lanka must diversify its markets, build trusted digital trade institutions, and balance between competing powers while keeping its ties with the US strong if it is to turn its post-crisis recovery into lasting prosperity in a fragmenting world order, three international experts said.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Sri Lanka must diversify its markets, build trusted digital trade institutions, and balance between competing powers while keeping its ties with the US strong if it is to turn its post-crisis recovery into lasting prosperity in a fragmenting world order, three international experts said.
content:
Sri Lanka must diversify its markets, build trusted digital trade institutions, and balance between competing powers while keeping its ties with the US strong if it is to turn its post-crisis recovery into lasting prosperity in a fragmenting world order, three international experts said.

International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) Global Honorary Chair Maria Fernanda Garza, Switzerland-based political consultant, campaign strategist, and political scientist Dr. Louis Perron, and former Sri Lankan Ambassador to the US, Mexico and Trinidad and Tobago Mahinda Samarasinghe were speaking at the 50th webinar organised by the Daily FT, Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), and the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka, together with Women in Management (WIM), the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors, the MBA Alumni Association of the University of Colombo, and Pioneer Institute of Business and Technology, on Saturday. The webinar was titled “In an Emerging New World Order, What Are Sri Lanka’s Options?” Garza, who visited Colombo in 2023 amid the economic crisis, said stability had since improved, growth had returned, and reforms were underway, but the world had changed profoundly. “We are not witnessing the end of globalisation, we are witnessing its transformation,” she said. She identified three opportunities. The first was diversification and regional integration, as over-dependence on a few markets, suppliers, or partners created vulnerability. Sri Lanka’s Indian Ocean location, its ties with India, and its connections across Asia, Europe, and the US allowed it to deepen its role in regional value chains, logistics, services, and higher-value exports. “The objective should not be to choose between competing economic powers, but to build diversified relationships that preserve economic opportunity and strategic flexibility,” she said. The second was digital transformation underpinned by institutional trust. Welcoming progress towards paperless customs, Garza cautioned that technology could make procedures faster without making them better. “The countries that benefit most will not necessarily be those that adopt technology fastest, but those that develop the institutional capacity to use it effectively,” she said. The third was renewing international cooperation, as predictable rules were essential infrastructure for smaller economies, the most exposed when cooperation gave way to power-based negotiations, she said. Samarasinghe, Ambassador in Washington for five years, said the US remained the world’s largest economy and importer, which was why leaders scrambled to strike deals after the Donald Trump Administration’s reciprocal tariffs of April 2025. Some 45 countries had since signed agreements under what he termed a carrot and stick approach, with Washington pursuing geopolitical objectives through trade talks. The sticks included surcharges on buyers of cheap Russian oil, since rolled back but liable to return, and a 40% surcharge on Vietnam over transshipment. The US also insisted on bilateral terms, full or near-full duty-free access for its exports, and US standards for its agricultural exports, he said. The carrot was a locked-in tariff rate, such as 15%, 19%, or 20%, shielded from fresh probes including Section 301 investigations, plus zero rating for thousands of goods. In return, partners made large pledges: the EU a non-binding $ 600 billion in investment and $ 750 billion in oil, gas, and nuclear fuel purchases, Japan $ 550 billion, Taiwan $ 500 billion, South Korea $ 300 billion, and India $ 500 billion. While tariff pressure had expedited alternatives such as the India-EU free trade agreement (FTA) after 17 years of talks, the US would remain the predominant economic force, he said. He urged Sri Lanka to keep exercising “smart options,” citing its role in Operation Prosperity Guardian in the Red Sea under President Ranil Wickremesinghe and the present Government’s handling of the Iranian ship issue, which the White House and the State Department praised for keeping the US informed while maintaining neutrality. “It is in Sri Lanka’s interest to have the best of relations with the US,” he said. Dr. Perron said Donald Trump’s return marked the end of sole US dominance after the Cold War, giving way to competing superpowers. A likely Democrat House majority after the midterms would deepen gridlock, leaving the world’s largest economy able to pass a budget only under threat of a Government shutdown, he said. Regional and medium powers such as Turkey, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, and Indonesia would grow more assertive amid shifting alliances. “You get a better deal from the superpowers if you do a balancing act as a country,” he said, adding that Wickremesinghe had done an outstanding job of this for Sri Lanka. The new order would be unstable, with regional wars likely, forcing many countries to follow the Israeli and Polish model of heavy defence spending while international law, the UN, and the World Trade Organisation (WTO) were sidelined, Dr. Perron warned. Citing the diverging fortunes of Colombia and Venezuela, Poland and Ukraine, and South and North Korea, he said the difference lay in the choices of political leadership.

headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: PM tells CNN IMF priorities align with Govt.’s own | Daily FT
summary_en: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has told CNN that several of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) priorities align with the Government’s own objectives, underpinning its decision to continue Sri Lanka’s IMF program despite her party’s earlier opposition.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has told CNN that several of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) priorities align with the Government’s own objectives, underpinning its decision to continue Sri Lanka’s IMF program despite her party’s earlier opposition.
content: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has told CNN that several of the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) priorities align with the Government’s own objectives, underpinning its decision to continue Sri Lanka’s IMF program despite her party’s earlier opposition. Dr. Amarasuriya said the Government had been able to discuss its concerns with the IMF, particularly on governance, corruption, and fiscal discipline. “When we came into power, the IMF agreement was already signed and we started working with them, and we found them approachable,” she told CNN’s Richard Quest of ‘Quest Means Business.’ Maintaining economic stability was among the administration’s immediate priorities following the election, she said, adding that the country had made considerable progress since the 2022 crisis. “We are doing remarkably well given what we’ve been through,” she said. The Prime Minister attributed the improvement primarily to fiscal management, financial discipline, efforts to address corruption and waste, and governance reforms. Two years into the administration, she said, the situation was ‘looking not too bad.’ Acknowledging that her party had opposed the IMF program due to Sri Lanka’s previous experiences with the institution, she said the Government had no choice but to continue it. We didn’t like it because we felt that our previous experiences with the IMF have not been great. This is not the first time we’ve entered an IMF program,” she said. She also acknowledged that the Government had faced pressure to demonstrate its ability to govern, saying many people had been waiting for it to fail. Dr. Amarasuriya also reaffirmed Sri Lanka’s commitment to geopolitical neutrality and non-alignment, saying conflicts such as the war in the Middle East ‘serve no one.’ Sri Lanka’s geographical position in the Indian Ocean made it important for the country to stay clear of geopolitical conflicts amid rising global tensions, she said. Avoiding entanglement in international power struggles was essential for its national interests and economic stability, she stressed, particularly as the country faces the impact of rising fuel prices and global energy costs. Acknowledging that maintaining balanced relations with major powers, including China, India, and the US, had historically been a key challenge for Sri Lanka’s foreign policy, she said aligning too closely with any single power had not worked to the country’s advantage. This, she said, underscored the importance of maintaining an independent foreign policy amid growing international tensions.

headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Sampath Bank’s Rs. 10 b debenture issue oversubscribed by 22.7% | Daily FT
summary_en: Sampath Bank PLC’s debenture issue was oversubscribed and closed at its maximum of Rs. 10 billion, having drawn applications worth Rs. 12.27 billion, with a small number of large-value payments made through Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) transfers and Letters of Guarantee accounting for nearly the entire amount.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Sampath Bank PLC’s debenture issue was oversubscribed and closed at its maximum of Rs. 10 billion, having drawn applications worth Rs. 12.27 billion, with a small number of large-value payments made through Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) transfers and Letters of Guarantee accounting for nearly the entire amount.
content: Sampath Bank PLC’s debenture issue was oversubscribed and closed at its maximum of Rs. 10 billion, having drawn applications worth Rs. 12.27 billion, with a small number of large-value payments made through Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) transfers and Letters of Guarantee accounting for nearly the entire amount. According to the Registrars to the issue, Central Depository Systems Ltd., the bank received 31 applications for 122.66 million debentures as at 22 October, against a maximum of 100 million debentures on offer, oversubscribing the issue by 22.7%. Excess demand amounted to Rs. 2.27 billion, or 22.66 million debentures. The issue comprised up to 100 million Basel III-compliant Tier 2 listed, rated, unsecured, subordinated, redeemable debentures with five-year (2026/2031) and seven-year (2026/2033) tenures, at a par value of Rs. 100 each. It was structured as an initial 70 million debentures to raise Rs. 7 billion, with an option to issue a further 30 million to raise Rs. 3 billion at the bank’s discretion in the event of an oversubscription. Tier 2 debentures count towards a bank’s regulatory capital. Their non-viability conversion feature allows them to be converted into ordinary shares if the bank is deemed non-viable, meaning holders absorb losses ahead of depositors. RTGS transfers, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL)-operated system for large-value interbank payments, were the dominant mode of payment. Eight applications paid via RTGS accounted for 80.5 million debentures worth Rs. 8.05 billion, or 65.6% of the total, an average of just over Rs. 1 billion per application. Payments by Letter of Guarantee came to Rs. 3.5 billion for 35 million debentures from three applications, or 28.5% of the total. In contrast, payments by bank drafts and cheques, which drew the highest number of applications at 20, amounted to Rs. 715.5 million for 7.16 million debentures, or 5.8% of the total value. By type, Type A debentures attracted 25 applications for 99.01 million debentures worth Rs. 9.9 billion. Of this, RTGS transfers accounted for Rs. 5.95 billion from six applications, Letters of Guarantee for Rs. 3.25 billion from two applications, and bank drafts and cheques for Rs. 700.5 million from 17 applications. Type B debentures drew six applications for 23.65 million debentures worth Rs. 2.37 billion. RTGS transfers accounted for Rs. 2.1 billion from two applications, a Letter of Guarantee for Rs. 250 million from one application, and bank drafts and cheques for Rs. 15 million from three applications.

headline_en: Ranil’s 10-point plan for Sri Lanka to survive new world order | Daily FT
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Ranil’s 10-point plan for Sri Lanka to survive new world order | Daily FT
summary_en: FORMER President Ranil Wickremesinghe has set out a 10-point plan for Sri Lanka to secure a place in an emerging world order, with rapid technological modernisation, membership of BRICS, and a stronger maritime role at its core.
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. FORMER President Ranil Wickremesinghe has set out a 10-point plan for Sri Lanka to secure a place in an emerging world order, with rapid technological modernisation, membership of BRICS, and a stronger maritime role at its core.
content: FORMER President Ranil Wickremesinghe has set out a 10-point plan for Sri Lanka to secure a place in an emerging world order, with rapid technological modernisation, membership of BRICS, and a stronger maritime role at its core. “If we do not do this, we will have no place in the new world order,” Wickremesinghe said, delivering the keynote at the 50th webinar organised by the Daily FT, Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), and the International Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka, together with Women in Management (WIM), the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors, the MBA Alumni Association of the University of Colombo, and Pioneer Institute of Business and Technology, on Saturday. The webinar was titled “In an Emerging New World Order, What Are Sri Lanka’s Options?” Among the requirements he set out were rapid technological modernisation resulting in a strong, competitive economy, making Sri Lanka a maritime logistics centre, close economic cooperation with India, and stronger relations with Bay of Bengal and other Southeast Asian countries, leading finally to regional integration. He also urged Sri Lanka to join BRICS, strengthen relations with the US, China, and Russia, as well as Japan, engage in transactional geopolitics, accelerate the work of the Colombo Security Conclave, and build a technologically advanced Navy with small and medium naval ships. “If you want to survive in this new global order, where technology plays this role and trade will certainly have an importance, either we have to go along this way or fade into insignificance like one of the small Pacific Isles,” he said. Wickremesinghe framed his proposals around Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address at the NDTV World Summit, which characterised the present as a world between orders, with one ending and another beginning. Modi had highlighted the weaponising of finance, trade, technology, and shipping as part of the new geopolitics, he noted, adding that post-World War II institutions were unable to intervene as they had not adapted to the changing order. Modi had also invoked Chanakya on the need to prevent Matsya Nyaya, where the strong swallow the weak. Citing a Goldman Sachs report, Wickremesinghe said Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data ownership, combined with dollar-dominated global financial markets, formed the basis of US dominance, while China, the other AI superpower, was seeking an alternative with BRICS members. “What we are witnessing today is a duopoly of AI and computing superpowers,” he said, adding that China and the US also led in space, ocean, and automation technologies, while India, the UK, France, Germany, Israel, Japan, and South Korea were developing their own. “We have to remember sovereignty today implies technology.” He said the decline of Western-led alliances was giving way to transactional geopolitics between the leading powers, and that Sri Lanka needed economic and social transformation based on technology-oriented modernisation, or it would be swallowed up. The Indian Ocean, he said, would be one of the centres of the new order alongside the emerging economies of Asia and Africa, strengthening its role as the main shipping artery between East and West, with immense undersea resources available for exploration. However, the US-Iran war had eroded the Indian Ocean’s status as a zone of peace and its freedom of navigation, he said, making it Sri Lanka’s interest to ensure that its two economic lifelines, the Suez Canal and the Gulf, remained fully operational. He urged policymakers not to ignore the Bay of Bengal as an economic region. Indonesia, projected to have the fourth or fifth largest GDP by 2050, would extend its influence, and Bangladesh would also emerge as an economic power, he said. Closer economic cooperation between Southeast Asia and Western China was producing the Chengdu-Chongqing corridor extending to Myanmar and Bangladesh, which he said would give China a second access to the Indian Ocean, this time through the Bay of Bengal. He also pointed to an economic region at Sri Lanka’s doorstep, a market of 600 million excluding India. Emerging technologies, including orbital maritime awareness satellites, hypersonic weapons, unmanned water vehicles, and drones, would play a major role in Indian Ocean security, he said, adding that protecting undersea cables in the region was a priority. On trade, Wickremesinghe, who said he had worked on agreements with Singapore and Thailand, named Indonesia, Malaysia, and Vietnam as the next targets. While Europe and the US remained important markets, Sri Lanka could not send more goods there and had to find markets elsewhere in Asia, “because that’s where the power is going to be.” “We are a hundred billion dollar GDP. We are so small. Most American corporations are bigger than that. So is Tata or Adani. We have to realise that and we must grow big,” he said. On the US midterm elections, he said foreign policy was unlikely to play a big role, and that both Vice President JD Vance and the Democrats appeared inclined to withdraw from global affairs, with the US relying instead on its financial and technological power. How the big powers and India drew their relations would determine “where and how we can play our pieces on the chessboard,” he said. “But to play the pieces on the chessboard, we have to become a strong economy. Otherwise, you are nowhere.” On AI, he warned of the emergence of trillion-dollar companies on both the US and Chinese sides, its impact on employment in India and Sri Lanka, and rising social tensions in the UK, France, and Germany if wealth concentrated among a handful of trillionaires. “We must know how to harness AI,” he said.
